rationale:
OWNER RULING 2026-09-03, recorded as RFC_060 §3g D2: 'fix the loancash wrong sentences.' Migration 738 (council-APPROVED cf7470b7) gave loancash.co.uk an evidence register and recorded three wrong live regulatory claims as `corrects_site_citation`, deliberately WITHOUT touching the served copy — rewriting published prose on an automated finding is authority the owner had withheld (695 precedent, bugs_open/320 §15). He has now lifted that hold FOR THESE THREE FINDINGS ON THIS SITE ONLY.

The repair goes through the framework rather than by hand, per two standing owner rulings: every site goes through the framework (2026-08-04) and the framework writes the content, not the session (2026-08-06). So this migration files four `content_rewrite` items (the £15 error appears on two pages) carrying the exact served wording, the exact required correction with the governing rule, and an acceptance test readable at the served bytes.

The most important of the three is not a cosmetic citation slip: on `guides/the-payday-loan-price-cap.html` and `guides/jargon-buster.html` the site frames the £15 default-fee cap as PER MISSED PAYMENT. CONC 5A.2.14R(1) caps it 'whether in relation to one breach or cumulatively in relation to multiple breaches of the agreement' — one £15 for the AGREEMENT. The site UNDERSTATES a borrower protection it exists to explain: a reader who missed two payments would accept a second £15 charge as lawful. It is not.

plan.summary: One additive migration filing 4 `content_rewrite` work items on loancash.co.uk, status `triaged`, handler `page-build-handler`. Three guards (site_id binds to the DOMAIN; the cited register must exist; refuse to double-file any of the four item_keys) and a DO/RAISE verify asserting 4 items, all 4 naming a page belonging to this site, and all 4 dispatchable and carrying current_value + suggestion + a substantive acceptance_test. Plus a ROLLBACK that CANCELS rather than deletes and refuses once anything has been claimed. No code changes; no served copy changed by this migration itself.
plan.risks:
(1) A `page_rerender` was queued on all four pages at 13:18 UTC today. A rerender regenerates from `content_data` and therefore RE-SHIPS the wrong wording byte for byte and completes successfully — it is not a repair and must not be read as one. Stated in every item's spec under `beware`.
(2) A completed `content_rewrite` is not a repaired artefact. `complete_work_item_acceptance_predicate.go`'s own note records that NO verifier is registered for `content_rewrite`, so its acceptance gate is inert for this type. Mitigated the only way available: each item carries an `acceptance_test` naming the served URL and the exact string that must or must not appear, so a human or a later sweep can check at the bytes.
(3) The framework rewrite may change MORE than the three sentences, since it regenerates a section rather than patching a clause. Accepted: it is the ruled mechanism, and the register now carries the correct statements (`claim`, `writer_line`) so the writer has the right facts to hand. Each `suggestion` names what must be KEPT as well as what must change, precisely to bound the collateral.
(4) `guides/stopping-payments-the-cpa-rules.html` is CORRECT on the two-attempt rule and must not be touched — it is the reference the loan-sharks page is to be made consistent WITH. Stated in every spec under `do_not_touch`.
(5) Dedup: `idx_swi_dedup` is UNIQUE on (site_id, item_key) for non-terminal statuses. All four keys are distinct; none exists on this site today; guard 3 refuses if any is already open. No `content_rewrite` was in a dispatchable state on any of the four pages when this was authored (measured 2026-09-03).

The domain-binding guard is new — it is the fix for the council's own low-severity objection on 738 (a mistyped uuid populates another site while every verify count still passes, being scoped to the same wrong id), now written into the shared method at RUNBOOK_lendzy §8e.

edits.rationale: CANCELS rather than DELETES: a claimed or handled item has history a delete would erase, and 'cancelled' is a terminal status `idx_swi_dedup` already excludes, so re-filing the same item_key later is not blocked. It REFUSES if any of the four has been claimed, completed or moved off 'triaged' — because once page-build-handler has acted the served copy may already have changed, and cancelling the item does not restore the old wording. That is a content decision, not a rollback, and the file says so.

grounded_in: OWNER RULING 2026-09-03, RFC_060 §3g D2: 'fix the loancash wrong sentences.' Lifts the 695 / bugs_open/320 §15 hold for these three findings on this site only.

CONC 5A.2.14R(1) verbatim, verified through cmd/fcaquotecheck 2026-09-03 with an absent control false in the same run: charges connected with a breach must not, 'whether in relation to one breach or cumulatively in relation to multiple breaches of the agreement', exceed £15.

Served copy, read at the artefact 2026-09-03 (all 30 pages crawled, invented-URL 404 control): 'that fee is capped at £15 and can only be charged once per missed payment, not once per day it stays missed' (the-payday-loan-price-cap.html); 'It is capped at £15, one-off, regardless of how many days late you are' (jargon-buster.html).

CONC 7.6.12R verbatim: a firm must not make a further request if it has done so 'on two previous occasions and those previous payment requests have been refused'. The string '£1' appears NOWHERE in the extracted visible text of CONC 7.6. Served copy: 'cannot take more than one payment attempt of over £1'. The site's own stopping-payments-the-cpa-rules.html states it correctly: 'A lender can attempt to collect a payment using your CPA twice.'

CONC 5A is titled 'Prohibition from entering into agreements for high-cost short-term credit' and contains no affordability rule; CONC 5.2A.4R is 'A firm must undertake a reasonable assessment of the creditworthiness of a customer before'. Served copy: 'the affordability checks set out under CONC 5A'.
